L: Rosa, 너는 빵 굽는 것을 잘하니?
Yes. I [started learning] to bake three years ago.
응. 나는 3년 전에 빵 굽는 것을 배우기 시작했어.
That's amazing. Your bread [must be] delicious.
Thanks. You can try some [if you want].
고마워. 원하면 좀 먹어 봐도 돼.
I'm studying coding. My goal is [to make] a game someday.
나는 코딩을 공부하고 있어. 내 목표는 언젠가 게임을 만드는 거야.
I see. [Are you good at] coding?
No, [I'm not good at] it yet. But I'm working hard.
아니, 아직 잘하지는 못해. 하지만 열심히 하고 있어.
That's good. [I'm sure] you will create a fun game one day.
좋네. 나는 네가 언젠가 재미있는 게임을 만들 거라고 확신해.
Hi, nice to meet you. I'm Jake, the new guitarist.
안녕, 만나서 반가워. 나는 새 기타리스트인 Jake야.
Nice to meet you. [Welcome to] our band! I'm Luna, and I [play the drums].
만나서 반가워. 우리 밴드에 온 걸 환영해! 나는 Luna이고, 드럼을 연주해.
Oh, I heard that you [are good at] playing the drums.
오, 네가 드럼을 잘 친다고 들었어.
That's nice to hear. I practice a lot.
그런 말을 들으니 좋다. 나는 연습을 많이 해.
Well, I [look forward to] playing with you.
음, 너와 함께 연주하는 것이 기대돼.
Yes, it will be fun! [I'm sure] we will make a great band.
응, 재미있을 거야! 나는 우리가 멋진 밴드가 될 거라고 확신해.
That's cool. [I'm sure] your voice [sounds wonderful].
멋지다. 나는 네 목소리가 훌륭하게 들릴 거라고 확신해.
Mia, 너는 글쓰기에 관심이 있지, 그렇지?
Yes. I want to be a writer, so I [keep a diary] every day.
응. 나는 작가가 되고 싶어서 매일 일기를 써.
That's great! [I'm sure] you will be a good writer.
멋지다! 나는 네가 좋은 작가가 될 거라고 확신해.
Thank you. [How about you], Suho? Do you enjoy writing?
고마워. 너는 어때, 수호야? 너는 글쓰기를 즐기니?
I enjoy it, but [I'm not good at] it.
Then [why don't you] join a writing class with me? There's a new one in the after-school program.
그럼 나와 함께 글쓰기 수업을 듣는 게 어때? 방과 후 프로그램에 새 수업이 있어.
Really? [Can you tell me more about] it?
정말? 그것에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
Sure. It [is held] every Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. in the school library. We can learn to write essays.
물론이지. 그 수업은 매주 수요일 오후 5시에 학교 도서관에서 열려. 우리는 에세이 쓰는 법을 배울 수 있어.
That sounds good. Let's [sign up] together.
I want to [take] the soccer class.
Okay. [Are you good at] playing soccer?
Great! [I'm sure] you will enjoy the class.
좋아! 나는 네가 그 수업을 즐길 거라고 확신해.
Jiwon, I saw your dance video on social media.
지원아, 나 소셜 미디어에서 네 춤 영상을 봤어.
Really? [What did you think of] it?
It was amazing. You [are really good at] dancing!
굉장했어. 너는 정말 춤을 잘 추는구나!
Thank you. I often make dance videos and [post] them.
고마워. 나는 자주 춤 영상을 만들어서 게시해.
That's great. Look, this video got a lot of comments. People said that they loved your dance moves.
멋지다. 봐, 이 영상에 댓글이 많이 달렸어. 사람들이 네 춤 동작이 정말 좋았다고 했어.
I'm [glad to hear] that. But I should practice more.
그 말을 들으니 기뻐. 하지만 나는 더 연습해야 해.
Actually, I'm practicing new dance moves these days. They are very difficult.
사실 나는 요즘 새로운 춤 동작들을 연습하고 있어. 그것들은 아주 어려워.
I see. [I'm sure] you will learn them quickly!
그렇구나. 나는 네가 그것들을 빨리 배울 거라고 확신해!
The person [who sits to my right] is Jinho.
내 오른쪽에 앉아 있는 사람은 진호야.
What did you write to him?
I wrote, “You [are good at] giving presentations.”
That's nice. How did he [become good at] it?
멋지다. 그는 어떻게 그것을 잘하게 되었니?
He [practiced speaking] in front of other people.
그는 다른 사람들 앞에서 말하는 것을 연습했어.
[I'm sure] he will be thankful for your message.
나는 그가 네 메시지에 고마워할 거라고 확신해.
Our Sports Day is coming, Siwoo! I'm excited.
우리 운동회가 다가오고 있어, 시우야! 나는 신나.
Hi, Yejin. What event are you going to [take part in]?
안녕, 예진아. 너는 어떤 종목에 참가할 거니?
I'm going to run a race.
Oh, me too. [Are you good at] running?
Yes. I have won races before.
응. 나는 전에 경주에서 우승한 적이 있어.
That's so cool. Actually, I'm worried about the race because [I'm not good at] running.
정말 멋지다. 사실 나는 달리기를 잘하지 못해서 경주가 걱정돼.
I can help you. [Why don't we] run together every morning?
내가 도와줄 수 있어. 우리 매일 아침 함께 달리는 게 어때?
No problem. [I'm sure] you will get better.
천만에. 나는 네가 더 나아질 거라고 확신해.

body.sub: The Dot ① A Blank Paper
lines: Art class was over, but Vashti still sat in her chair.
Her paper was blank.
Her teacher leaned over and looked at it.
“Ah! It is a polar bear in a snowstorm,” she said.
“That’s funny!” said Vashti. “I CAN’T draw!”
Her teacher smiled. “Just make a mark.”

body.sub: The Dot ② Just Make a Mark
lines: Vashti picked up a marker and drew a small dot on the paper.
“Here it is!”
Her teacher picked up the paper and looked at it carefully.
“Hmmm.” She pushed the paper toward Vashti and asked her to sign it.
Vashti thought for a moment.
“Well, maybe I can’t draw, but I CAN sign my name.”

body.sub: The Dot ③ In a Frame
lines: The next day, Vashti was surprised to see something in a frame on the wall of the art classroom.
It was her little dot!
“I can make a better dot than that!” Vashti said.
She got a brush and started painting.
A red dot. A purple dot. A yellow dot. A blue dot.
Then she mixed blue and yellow together.
She discovered that she could make a green dot.
Vashti kept experimenting.
She painted lots of little dots in many colors.
“If I can make little dots, I can make big dots, too.”
All of the dots that she painted looked beautiful together on the paper.

body.sub: The Dot ⑤ The Art Show
lines: At the school art show a few weeks later, everyone loved Vashti’s paintings.
A little boy looked up at her.
“You’re a really great artist.
I want to paint like you,” he said.
“I bet you can,” said Vashti.
“Me? No, not me. I CAN’T draw!”
Vashti smiled.
She handed the boy a blank sheet of paper and told him to draw a line.
The pencil which the boy held shook as he drew.
Vashti looked at the boy’s line.
And then she said ... “Sign it.”
